newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers adopt proposals for Delta scandal.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers adopt proposals for Delta scandal.

text.p: Greek stockbrokers agreed to ask the national economy ministry to nullify billions of drachmas in trades in recent days between Delta Securities, charged with alleged fraud, and 11 other brokers, their association said.
It was unclear whether the bourse, closed for two days by the Delta scandal, would open for regular business on Tuesday.
Representatives of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) headed straight to a meeting with deputy economy minister Apostolos Fotiades to seek his approval for the deal.
SMEHA, representing the 65 securities firms registered to trade on the Athens bourse, hammered out the proposals to settle the Delta scandal during an earlier emergency session.
The proposals seek to nullify trades with Delta Securities which took place from October 30 -- the trade date for which it issued bad cheques.
Delta set off the fiasco at the bourse last week after failing to provide funds to the clearing house to settle 2.6 billion drachmas in trades.
SMEHA members then refused to trade, effectively closing the bourse on Friday and Monday until the settlement issue was resolved.

The proposals would readjust the positions of all other members vis-a-vis the clearing house based on the decision to have the disputed trades with Delta reversed. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
